title: Pantograph Not Raising / Drops Immediately
symptoms: ZPT operated to position 1 or 2, but Pantograph remains down on roof.
Auxiliary reservoir gauge (RS) shows low pressure (< 6.0 kg/cm²).
Diagnostic display message: 'Pantograph not raised' or 'Panto interlock failed'.
Cab indicator lamp LS-PT remains dark or does not extinguish.
probable_causes: Auxiliary reservoir (RS) pressure less than 6.0 kg/cm².
Control electronics / battery voltage < 90V (UBA voltmeter).
Earthing switch HOM handle not locked in vertical 'Working' position.
High Tension (HT) compartment doors or roof hatch not fully locked (IG38 key interlock open).
Panto cut-out cock (COC 130) on pneumatic panel closed or leaking.
Pressure switch 269.4 / 269.6 defective or electrical connector loose.
preliminary_checks: Check Battery Voltmeter (UBA) ≥ 90V.
Check RS gauge in machine room: must be ≥ 6.5 kg/cm². If low, start Baby Compressor (MCPA) switch 172.2.
Inspect both Machine Room HT compartment doors and ensure mechanical key interlocks are firmly locked.
Verify BL key is inserted and turned to position '1'.
remedial_steps: 1. Check RS pressure on gauge in Machine Room-2. If pressure is below 6.0 kg/cm², run Auxiliary Compressor (MCPA) using switch BLCP or manual MCPA toggle until RS pressure reaches 7.0 kg/cm².
2. Check battery voltage on voltmeter UBA in Cab-1/Cab-2. If below 90V, recharge via external charger or check battery circuit breaker 110.
3. Inspect Earthing Switch (HOM) handle in Machine Room. Ensure the handle is vertical and key IG-38 is in 'Operating' position, with yellow safety latch engaged.
4. Check Panto selector switch (ZPT): Change selection from 'Rear' to 'Front' or 'Both' (Position 1 -> 2).
5. Inspect Panto Solenoid Valve (VEPT) in pneumatic panel. Check whether the manual override push-pin on VEPT can be pressed to test air flow to roof.
6. Check circuit breaker 127.11 (Electronics/Panto Control) on HB1 panel. If tripped, reset once.
7. If Panto still does not raise, isolate defective Panto via 130 COC and attempt raising the alternate pantograph.
safety_precautions: Never climb on loco roof under live 25 kV OHE. Ensure 100% discharge through HOM earthing switch before opening HT mesh. If section detention exceeds 10 minutes, inform TLC (22328) / PCNL (22666 / 22667).
contact_instruction: Contact TLC (22328) or PCNL (22666/22667) if RS air leakage persists or mechanical damage is observed on panto pan carbon strips.

flowchart.title: 3-Phase Pantograph Raising Decision Flowchart
flowchart.summary: Step-by-step diagnostic sequence to identify pneumatic, electrical, and interlock reasons when Pantograph fails to raise or drops immediately.

steps.title: Fault Detected: Panto Fails to Raise
steps.desc: ZPT switch pressed to UP (pos 1), but Panto does not rise or drops immediately. No OHE tension indication.

steps.title: Check Auxiliary Reservoir (RS) Pressure
steps.desc: Examine the RS pressure gauge in Machine Room No. 2. Is RS pressure equal to or greater than 5.2 kg/cm²?

steps.title: Start Baby Compressor (MCPA)
steps.desc: Switch ON Auxiliary Compressor (MCPA) toggle switch on panel SB-2. Run MCPA until RS pressure builds up to at least 6.0 kg/cm².

steps.title: Verify Emergency Stop & IG-38 Key Interlocks
steps.desc: Are both Cab Emergency Stop buttons released and Key IG-38 in Cab-1 locked in vertical position?

steps.title: Select Alternate Pantograph via Switch 125
steps.desc: Rotate Panto Selector Switch 125 on Pneumatic Panel to position 1 (Panto-1) or position 2 (Panto-2) instead of Auto.

steps.title: Twist Release Emergency Stop & Reset MCB 127.12
steps.desc: Twist and release Emergency Stop buttons in both cabs. Inspect and reset MCB 127.12 in Auxiliary Cubicle HB-2.

steps.title: Panto Raised Successfully
steps.desc: Pantograph makes firm contact with OHE. U-meter registers 25 kV. Proceed with closing Main Circuit Breaker (VCB).

steps.title: Escalation: Contact TLC
steps.desc: If Panto still fails to raise, visually inspect carbon strip and roof equipment for physical damage. Contact TLC on 22328.

title: Circuit Breaker (DJ / VCB) Fails to Close or Trips Immediately
symptoms: BLDJ pressed to close, but LSDJ remains permanently glowing.
VCB closing sound heard momentarily then trips with loud exhaust.
Diagnostic Screen displays 'Fault in Main Circuit' or 'OHE Voltage out of range'.
Voltmeter U shows 0 kV or < 17.5 kV.
probable_causes: OHE catenary voltage abnormal (< 17.5 kV or > 30.0 kV) or neutral section encountered.
Emergency Stop push button (BPEMS) pressed in either Cab-1 or Cab-2.
Control reservoir (RS) air pressure below 6.5 kg/cm² for VCB operation.
Transformer oil pressure / temperature protection relay (MPH / TF Oil) tripped.
Primary over-current or earth fault relay (78 / 86) tripped.
Circuit breaker 127.1 (VCB control) tripped on SB1 panel.
preliminary_checks: Look at catenary voltmeter (U): verify OHE voltage is between 19 kV and 27.5 kV.
Ensure Emergency Stop Button (BPEMS in Cab-1 & Cab-2, BVEB in rear cab) is fully released.
Check Control Reservoir (RS) pressure ≥ 6.5 kg/cm².
Check if any Subsystem (SS01, SS02) shows permanent isolation on DDU screen.
remedial_steps: 1. Verify OHE voltage on voltmeter (U). If below 17.5 kV or zero, contact TLC (22328) to confirm power supply from Traction Substation (TSS).
2. Check Emergency Stop Push Buttons (BPEMS) in both cabs. Turn clockwise and release if latched.
3. Open Machine Room and inspect SB1 panel: Verify MCB 127.1 (VCB Control), MCB 127.22, and MCB 127.91 are ON. If tripped, reset once.
4. Check transformer oil level gauges on both sides of transformer tank. Verify oil level is between MIN and MAX marks.
5. Press fault acknowledge button on DDU (Diagnostic Display Unit) screen. Wait for self-test sequence (Self-test count 0 to 1).
6. Insert BL key, set to '1', raise pantograph (ZPT=1), wait for U voltmeter to show ~25 kV, then press BLDJ for 2-3 seconds.
7. If VCB still does not close, isolate Subsystem-01 via screen and attempt closing under degraded mode as per DDU prompt.
safety_precautions: Do not attempt repeated BLDJ closing more than 3 times within 5 minutes to prevent burning of VCB closing coil. Confirm track clearance before stepping down to inspect underframe.
contact_instruction: Immediately advise TLC (22328) / PCNL (22666 / 22667) if VCB trips with an audible flash or if relay 78 indicates transformer primary over-current.

flowchart.title: 3-Phase VCB / DJ Closing & Holding Flowchart
flowchart.summary: Procedural decision tree to diagnose VCB closing failures, OHE voltage boundary errors, and node interlock trips.

steps.title: Fault Detected: VCB Fails to Close
steps.desc: BLDJ pressed to close VCB, but VCB does not close or trips out immediately. LSDJ lamp remains continuously glowing.

steps.title: Check OHE Voltage on U-Meter
steps.desc: Check line voltmeter (U-Meter) on Cab Desk. Is OHE line voltage within permissible limits (17.5 kV to 30.0 kV)?

steps.title: Verify Cab Handles & Press BLDJ
steps.desc: Ensure Reverser handle (MP) is in '0' (Neutral) and TE/BE throttle is at '0'. Press and hold BLDJ for 2-3 seconds until LSDJ extinguishes.

steps.title: OHE Voltage Deficit -> Inform TLC
steps.desc: OHE No Tension or out-of-range voltage. Contact Traction Loco Control (TLC: 22328 / PCNL: 22666). Await power restoration.

steps.title: Did VCB Close and LSDJ Extinguish?
steps.desc: Listen for heavy pneumatic latching sound of VCB and observe LSDJ indication on desk.

steps.title: VCB Successfully Latched
steps.desc: VCB is holding. Auxiliary converters BUR-1/2/3 start in sequence. Loco is ready to develop tractive effort.

steps.title: Check MCBs 127.1 / 127.2 & Soft Reset CE
steps.desc: Check and reset MCB 127.1 (HB-1) & MCB 127.2 (HB-2). Ensure MR pressure >= 6.4 kg/cm² on switch 269.6. Perform soft restart of CE (Key D OFF for 5 min).

steps.title: VCB Actuator Failure -> Call TLC
steps.desc: If VCB fails to close after CE restart, internal pneumatic valve or vacuum bottle fault suspected. Call TLC (22328).

title: Auxiliary Converter Fault (BUR-1 / BUR-2 / BUR-3 Tripping)
symptoms: Cab annunciator buzzer sounds with glowing yellow/red warning lamp.
Screen displays: 'Fault in Auxiliary Converter 1/2/3' or 'BUR tripped'.
Oil pumps (MPH) or cooling blowers (OCB, TMB) stop or run in degraded mode.
Reduced cooling capacity or compressor not loading.
probable_causes: Overcurrent or DC-link overvoltage in Auxiliary Converter (BUR 1, 2, or 3).
Earth fault on 415V three-phase auxiliary motor circuit.
Cooling blower motor seized or bearing jammed.
Control MCB tripped on HB1 or HB2 panel.
Contactor 52/1, 52/2, 52/3 sticking in open or closed position.
preliminary_checks: Observe diagnostic display screen to identify which BUR has tripped (BUR-1, BUR-2, or BUR-3).
Check auxiliary converter busbar contactor indications on DDU screen.
Inspect HB1 and HB2 panels in Machine Room for tripped miniature circuit breakers.
remedial_steps: 1. Acknowledge fault on display screen by pressing 'ACK' button.
2. Check if automatic bus reconfiguration took place (BUR redundancy management). In modern 3-Phase locos, if one BUR fails, the remaining two BURs automatically share auxiliary loads.
3. If automatic reconfiguration failed, bring throttle to '0', open VCB (BLDJ), lower panto, switch off BL key, wait 2 minutes for DC link capacitors to discharge.

4. Enter machine room and check HB1 and HB2 panels: Inspect MCB 59.1 (Oil Cooling Blower 1), 59.2 (Oil Cooling Blower 2), 53.1 (Traction Motor Blower 1), 53.2 (TMB 2), 62.1 (Transformer Oil Pump 1), 62.2 (TF Oil Pump 2), 63.1 (Converter Oil Pump 1), 63.2 (Converter Oil Pump 2).
5. If any auxiliary motor MCB is tripped, isolate that specific motor's breaker, restart loco (BL key to '1', Panto up, VCB closed), and clear section with restricted tractive effort.
6. If entire BUR module is burnt or smoking, mechanically isolate the converter module via screen and inform TLC (22328).
safety_precautions: Operating with one isolated cooling blower requires monitoring traction motor and oil temperatures continuously. If oil temperature exceeds 84°C, stop the train in a safe block section.
contact_instruction: Advise TLC (22328) immediately regarding isolated BUR and reduced traction capability.

flowchart.title: 3-Phase Auxiliary Converter (BUR 1/2/3) Tripping Flowchart
flowchart.summary: Automatic reconfiguration check and soft restart sequence for auxiliary converter bus-tie contactors.

steps.title: Auxiliary Converter Fault Displayed
steps.desc: Diagnostic screen displays 'Auxiliary Converter Fault' (F0201P1 / F0202P1). Warning lamp LSFI blinks.

steps.title: Identify Failed BUR Subsystem on Screen
steps.desc: Navigate to Subsystem 02 on DDS screen. Identify whether BUR-1, BUR-2, or BUR-3 has tripped.

steps.title: Did Auto Reconfiguration Succeed?
steps.desc: Check if bus-tie contactors 52/1, 52/3 automatically closed to power blowers through remaining 2 BURs.

steps.title: 2-BUR Mode Operational
steps.desc: Reconfiguration successful. All essential cooling blowers running. Continue train operation at permitted load. Log in Loco Book.

steps.title: Stop Train Safely & Perform CE Restart
steps.desc: Bring train to complete stop. Lower panto and open VCB. Turn Control Electronics Key 'D' to OFF. Wait 5 full minutes.

steps.title: Re-energise CE & Re-raise Panto
steps.desc: Turn Key 'D' to ON, raise panto and close VCB. Verify whether BURs reboot and latch normally.

steps.title: Persistent BUR Lockout -> Call TLC
steps.desc: If BUR trips again and blowers do not run, do NOT notch up traction to prevent motor overheating. Inform TLC on 22328.

title: Traction Converter Fault & Bogie Isolation (Switch 154)
symptoms: Loco tractive effort drops by approximately 50%.
Screen displays: 'Fault in Traction Converter 1' (or 2) and 'Bogie 1 / Bogie 2 Isolated'.
Line contactor open indication on DDU screen.
Acceleration is sluggish; higher current drawn on operational bogie.
probable_causes: Traction Converter DC-link short circuit or ground fault.
GTO / IGBT gate drive unit failure or power semiconductor breakdown.
Converter cooling water pressure low or cooling pump tripped.
Traction Motor speed sensor (pulse generator) failure on one axle.
Pre-charging contactor 15.1 / 15.2 failed to close.
preliminary_checks: Check DDU screen for specific Bogie status (Bogie 1 = Axles 1, 2, 3; Bogie 2 = Axles 4, 5, 6).
Check converter cooling water level on sight glasses on SR1 / SR2 tank.
Verify position of Bogie Cut-out Rotary Switch 154 on SB1 panel.
remedial_steps: 1. Bring master throttle to '0' position.
2. Press 'ACK' on screen to clear transient disturbances.
3. Open VCB by pressing BLDJ, wait 10 seconds, then reclose VCB and advance throttle gently to 20% to check if tractive effort recovers.
4. If traction converter trips repeatedly, bring loco to a halt at the next station platform or loop line.
5. Open VCB, lower pantograph, turn BL key to '0'.
6. Go to Machine Room SB1 panel: Locate rotary switch 154 (Bogie Cut-out Switch).
- Position 'Norm': Both Bogies working.
- Position 'I': Bogie 1 Isolated (Only Bogie 2 working).
- Position 'II': Bogie 2 Isolated (Only Bogie 1 working).
7. Turn switch 154 to isolate the defective bogie. Restart the loco. Confirm message on screen: 'Loco working with Bogie Isolated'.
8. Clear the section with 50% power. Observe grade and starting restrictions with heavy freight or passenger loads.
safety_precautions: With one bogie isolated, dynamic (regenerative) braking is also reduced by 50%. Apply train air brakes (A-9) earlier on down-gradients to prevent overspeed.
contact_instruction: Immediately log bogie isolation with TLC (22328) and enter details in the Loco Log Book.

flowchart.title: 3-Phase Traction Converter Isolation (Switch 154) Flowchart
flowchart.summary: Procedural guide to isolate a defective traction bogie and operate on 50% tractive effort.

steps.title: Traction Converter Failure Displayed
steps.desc: DDS alerts 'Traction Converter-1 Fault' (F0301P1) or 'Traction Converter-2 Fault' (F0401P1). Loss of tractive effort in one bogie.

steps.title: Bring Train to Halt on Level Track
steps.desc: Safely stop train. Lower panto and open VCB. Turn Control Electronics Key 'D' to OFF position.

steps.title: Locate Bogie Isolation Switch 154
steps.desc: Enter Machine Room No. 1 and locate rotary Switch 154 on Auxiliary Cubicle SB-1.

steps.title: Select Faulty Bogie to Isolate
steps.desc: Rotate Switch 154 to isolate the failed converter identified on DDS:

steps.title: Reboot CE & Energise Healthy Bogie
steps.desc: Turn Key 'D' to ON, raise panto, close VCB. DDS will acknowledge isolation and show healthy bogie in green.

steps.title: Single-Bogie 50% TE Traction Restored
steps.desc: Locomotive can operate on 50% tractive effort. Clear block section safely to nearest junction. Inform TLC on 22328.

title: Vigilance Control Device (VCD) Penalty Brake Application & Reset
symptoms: VCD visual warning lamp flashes on desk for 8 seconds, followed by audio buzzer for 8 seconds.
If unacknowledged, Emergency / Penalty brake applies automatically.
Brake Pipe (BP) pressure drops from 5.0 kg/cm² to 2.8 - 3.0 kg/cm².
Throttle cuts to zero and traction power is cut off automatically.
DDU screen displays: 'VCD Penalty Brake Applied'.
probable_causes: Loco Pilot did not perform any vigilance activity within 60 seconds (no throttle change, horn, sanding, or VCD foot pedal pressed).
VCD foot pedal micro-switch failed or stuck open.
VCD reset pushbutton on assistant's side defective.
Speed sensor false pulse triggering VCD at standstill.
preliminary_checks: Ensure train has come to a complete halt before attempting reset.
Check that master controller throttle is brought back to '0'.
Verify BP pressure gauge reading (showing drop).
remedial_steps: 1. Bring throttle handle (TE/BE) immediately to '0' position.
2. Place Auto Brake Valve handle (A-9) to Emergency / Lap position.
3. Wait for the train to come to a complete stop. Wait for minimum 160 seconds (mandatory internal penalty lock duration on standard VCD systems).
4. Ensure VCD foot pedal is fully released and not jammed with footwear or dirt.
5. Press the illuminated VCD Reset Push Button on the loco pilot's desk or assistant desk for 2-3 seconds.
6. Observe Brake Pipe (BP) pressure gauge: BP will begin charging back to 5.0 kg/cm².
7. Return A-9 handle to 'RUN' position.
8. Verify DDU screen shows 'VCD Normal' and tractive effort interlock is released.
9. If VCD resets successfully, continue journey. Be vigilant to operate foot pedal or horn every 50 seconds.

10. If VCD is defective and keeps penalty braking repeatedly with no fault of crew, isolate VCD by turning VCD Isolating Cock on pneumatic panel or toggle VCD bypass switch in SB1 panel with TLC permission.
safety_precautions: Isolating VCD requires formal approval from TLC/Officer. Never wedge or tie down the VCD foot pedal with weights, as modern systems detect continuous press as a tamper and apply brakes.
contact_instruction: Record VCD penalty brake application in the Loco Log Book. If VCD was isolated due to hardware failure, communicate immediately to TLC (22328).

flowchart.title: Vigilance Control Device (VCD) Penalty Reset Flowchart
flowchart.summary: Mandatory safety sequence to clear VCD penalty brake application and recharge brake pipe.

steps.title: VCD Penalty Brake Applied
steps.desc: Flashing VCD indicator and buzzer unacknowledged for 76 seconds. BP exhausts automatically to 2.8 - 3.0 kg/cm².

steps.title: Throttle & Reverser to '0' Neutral
steps.desc: Immediately bring TE/BE throttle handle to '0'. Move Reverser handle (MP) to '0' (Neutral).

steps.title: Ensure Complete Train Halt
steps.desc: Wait for train to come to a standstill. NEVER attempt to reset VCD penalty while train is rolling!

steps.title: Wait 160 Seconds Penalty Lock Period
steps.desc: Observe cab clock / watch. Wait exactly 160 seconds for internal electronic penalty timer to expire.

steps.title: Press VCD Reset Switch (237.1)
steps.desc: Press VCD Reset Push Button Switch 237.1 on Assistant Loco Pilot's desk for 2-3 seconds.

steps.title: Does Brake Pipe (BP) Recharge to 5.0 kg/cm²?
steps.desc: Watch duplex air pressure gauge on cab desk. Does BP pressure build up smoothly to 5.0 kg/cm²?

steps.title: Penalty Cleared & Normal Operation Resumed
steps.desc: Brakes released across the train. Resume normal journey. Enter penalty details in VCD Log Book.

steps.title: Isolate Cock 74 & Trip MCB 127.9/1
steps.desc: Isolate VCD Pneumatic Cock (Cock 74) on Pneumatic Panel. Switch OFF MCB 127.9/1 in SB-1. Advise TLC (22328).

title: Brake Pipe (BP) & Feed Pipe (FP) Pressure Deficit / Continuous Exhaust
symptoms: BP pressure cannot be charged to 5.0 kg/cm²; hovers around 3.5 - 4.2 kg/cm².
Continuous hiss or air exhaust sound from relay valve or emergency flap.
Air Flow Indicator (AFI) needle shows very high air leakage (> 5 units).
Main Reservoir (MR) pressure dropping rapidly despite both compressors running.
probable_causes: Rear cab A-9 handle not placed in 'Neutral' or emergency exhaust cock open.
Air brake pipe angle cock between loco and train uncoupled or damaged gasket.
Alarm Chain Pulling (ACP) in passenger coaches or train parting.
Brake pipe isolating cock (COC 70 / 74) on pneumatic brake panel in wrong position.
E-70 / CCB brake controller solenoid valve failure.
preliminary_checks: Check MR pressure ≥ 8.5 kg/cm². Both main compressors (MCP1 & MCP2) must be in AUTO mode.
Verify A-9 handle in rear cab is locked in NEUTRAL position and lead/trail selector is set to TRAIL in rear cab.
Observe AFI (Air Flow Indicator) gauge.
remedial_steps: 1. Put Compressor switch BLCP to 'MANUAL' (position 1) to force both main compressors to run simultaneously.
2. Check Auto Brake Controller (A-9) in driving cab: Move to 'RELEASE' position for 5 seconds, then return to 'RUN'.
3. Go to rear cab: Verify A-9 is locked, Guard Emergency Valve (RS valve) is tightly shut, and BPEMS is released.
4. Enter Machine Room: Check Pneumatic Panel (E-70 or CCB system):
- Confirm Cut-out Cock 70 (BP Charging Cock) is open (parallel to pipe).
- Confirm Cut-out Cock 74 (Emergency Exhaust) is closed.
- On CCB locos, check Lead/Trail switch on display unit is set to 'LEAD'.
5. If BP is still not charging, close Cock 70 on loco front buffer and observe if loco BP charges to 5.0 kg/cm²:
- If loco charges to 5.0 kg/cm², the leakage is in the train rake (ACP, broken pipe, or open drain cock). Send ALP with Guard to walk the rake.
- If loco itself does not charge to 5.0 kg/cm², problem is inside loco brake panel. Cycle CCB circuit breaker 127.19.
6. After rectifying train leak, reopen angle cock slowly, ensure BP reaches 5.0 kg/cm² and FP reaches 6.0 kg/cm².
safety_precautions: Never move the train if BP pressure is below 4.8 kg/cm² or FP below 5.8 kg/cm². Mandatory brake continuity test must be performed before restarting.
contact_instruction: Advise TLC (22328) and Section Controller if train detention exceeds scheduled halt.

flowchart.title: Brake Pipe (BP) Deficit & Exhaust Troubleshooting Flowchart
flowchart.summary: Pneumatic diagnostic flow to identify train pipe ruptures, cock positions, and emergency valve leaks.

steps.title: Brake Pipe Pressure Deficit Detected
steps.desc: BP pressure drops below 5.0 kg/cm² or continuous heavy hiss of air exhaust heard from cab or train rake.

steps.title: Verify A-9 Handle & Lead/Trail Switch
steps.desc: Is A-9 automatic brake handle in 'RUN' position and Lead/Trail switch set properly to 'Lead'?

steps.title: Check Emergency Valve Cock (Cock 70)
steps.desc: Inspect Assistant Loco Pilot's Emergency Brake Cock (Cock 70) in both cabs. Ensure handle is tightly closed.

steps.title: Correct A-9 Handle Position
steps.desc: Set A-9 handle firmly in RUN position. In trailing/banking cabs, ensure A-9 is pinned in Neutral.

steps.title: Check MR Main Reservoir Pressure
steps.desc: Is Main Reservoir (MR) pressure between 8.5 and 10.0 kg/cm²? Are main compressors charging normally?

steps.title: Train Rake vs Locomotive Leakage Check
steps.desc: Close BP angle cock at rear of locomotive. Does loco BP charge to 5.0 kg/cm²?

options.label: YES (Loco OK -> Leakage is in Train Rake)

steps.title: Check Compressors & Drain Cocks
steps.desc: Check BLCP switch is in 'AUTO' or 'MAN'. Inspect auto-drain valves and moisture separator for continuous blowing.

steps.title: Examine Train Rake with Guard
steps.desc: Coordinate with Guard: walk the rake to identify uncoupled hose, open passenger alarm chain (ACP), or open guard van valve.

steps.title: Check Distributor Valve & IP Valve
steps.desc: Inspect C3W distributor valve isolating cock on pneumatic panel. If blowing continuously, tap gently or isolate.

steps.title: Brake Pipe Pressure Restored to 5.0 kg/cm²
steps.desc: Leak sealed. BP holds steady at 5.0 kg/cm², FP at 6.0 kg/cm². Perform brake feel test and proceed.

title: Hotel Load Converter (HOG) Tripping / Failure to Power Passenger Rake
symptoms: Train coach lights and air conditioning turn off or trip to battery emergency mode.
HOG indicator lamp on desk extinguishes; audible alarm on HOG control box.
Display screen indicates: 'HOG Converter 1 / Converter 2 Tripped'.
DG set (EOG power car) has to be cranked by train electrical staff.
probable_causes: Earth leakage or overcurrent in rake 750V feeder lines.
Loose or dislodged UIC Hotel Load couplers between loco and first coach.
HOG inverter module over-temperature.
Filter contactor or pre-charging resistor failure in HOG cubicle.
Phase imbalance across R, Y, B lines feeding train coaches.
preliminary_checks: Check DDU screen for specific HOG error message (Earth Fault, Overload, or Inverter Trip).
Verify OHE voltage is stable between 21.5 kV and 27 kV.
Ensure train electrical supervisor (Escorting Staff) is contacted.
remedial_steps: 1. Press HOG Fault Reset push button on HOG control panel in Machine Room-2.
2. Ask train electrical escorting staff to verify if coach feeder breakers in the guard/power car tripped on overcurrent.
3. If HOG tripped on Earth Leakage:
- Inform Train Lighting (TL/AC) staff to isolate defective coach feeder circuit.
- Reset earth leakage relay on HOG panel.
4. If one HOG converter module (e.g. HOG-1) has failed, check whether HOG-2 can take the entire hotel load (upto 500 kVA limit).
5. Re-operate HOG ON switch on driving desk: Press 'BLHO' switch.
6. If HOG repeatedly trips and cannot be restored within 10 minutes, advise Guard and train escorting staff to start EOG Power Car Diesel Generator to prevent passenger discomfort.
safety_precautions: Never touch 750V IV couplers or UIC jumpers without opening HOG breakers and verifying zero voltage indicator on power panel.
contact_instruction: Log HOG failure with TLC (22328) and Power Control (PCNL - 22666 / 22667). Record time of switching over to EOG generator.

flowchart.title: Hotel Load Converter (HOG) Troubleshooting Flowchart
flowchart.summary: Checklist sequence to restore power to train coaching air conditioning and lighting.

steps.title: HOG Tripped / Passenger Rake Power Off
steps.desc: Hotel Load Converter trips. AC and lights in coaching stock shut down. DDS shows HOG Inverter Fault.

steps.title: Inspect UIC IV Coupler Cable
steps.desc: Visually examine Hotel Load IV couplers between loco and front power car for loose pins or water ingress.

steps.title: Open VCB & Reset HOG MCB
steps.desc: Open VCB. Enter Machine Room and locate HOG Control Cubicle. Reset tripped HOG control circuit breakers.

steps.title: Re-close VCB & Press HOG ON
steps.desc: Re-close VCB. Press HOG ON push button on Driver Desk. Observe HOG voltage build-up on display.

steps.title: Does HOG Supply 750V 3-Phase to Rake?
steps.desc: Check HOG panel voltmeter. Is 750V AC active and coaching supply restored?

steps.title: HOG Normal Operation Restored
steps.desc: Passenger coaches powered via locomotive. Advise Train Superintendent. Proceed on run.

steps.title: Start DG Power Car (EOG Mode) -> Call TLC
steps.desc: Internal HOG inverter failure. Advise Guard & AC staff to start DG set in Power Car. Inform TLC (22328).

title: Speedometer (SPM) Failure / Frozen Display / Zero Speed Indication
symptoms: Speedometer needle or digital display remains at '0 km/h' while train is running.
Speed display frozen at a fixed reading.
Speedometer memory card error LED blinking red on recorder unit (MRT 922 / Telpro).
Distance counter not advancing.
probable_causes: Pulse generator (PG) axle-end sensor disconnected, loose cable, or mechanical breakage.
Speedometer recorder unit power supply interrupted.
MCB 127.91 tripped on SB1 panel.
Internal firmware crash of digital recorder unit.
preliminary_checks: Compare Speedometer display in Cab-1 with Speedometer display in Cab-2.
Check auxiliary speed display on DDU / RTIS / Kavach unit if fitted.
Inspect axle-box pulse generator cable on Axle-2 or Axle-4.
remedial_steps: 1. Check MCB 127.91 (Speedometer / Recorder power supply) on SB1 panel. If tripped, reset once.
2. For Medha / Telpro / Laxven units: Press System Reset button on the face of the recorder unit in Machine Room.
3. If speed sensor 1 is defective, toggle sensor selector switch (Sensor 1 / Sensor 2) on the speedometer panel to switch to redundant axle pulse generator.
4. If speedometer display remains completely blank or dead, record the exact kilometre and time in the log book.
5. Crew must observe speed by cross-checking with RTIS / GPS speed on CMS tablet, stopwatch against kilometre posts, or speed displayed on DDU diagnostic unit.
6. Advise Guard to inform next station master and regulate speed strictly as per caution orders and maximum permissible speed (MPS).
safety_precautions: In case of total speedometer failure, run with extreme caution, never exceed sectional MPS, and use telephone/CUG to report to TLC.
contact_instruction: Advise TLC (22328) at the next stopping station. Memo must be given to CCC at destination.

title: DJ Not Closing (BLDJ Pressed, LSDJ Remains Glowing Continuously)
symptoms: BLDJ pressed with BLRDJ held, but pilot lamp LSDJ stays lit.
Auxiliary voltmeter UBA shows battery voltage but no DJ closing thud heard.
Pantograph is raised and OHE voltmeter shows 25 kV.
Relay Q44 and Q118 target status not engaging.
probable_causes: Control Reservoir (RS) pressure below 6.5 kg/cm².
Emergency push button BVEB pressed in either cab.
BL key not properly engaged in position '1' or BLDJ switch contact carbonized.
Relay Q44 not energizing due to open interlock.
Relay Q118 de-energized due to tripped safety relay (QLM, QRSI, QOP, QOA).
Control fuse CCPT (16A) or CCBA (35A) blown.
preliminary_checks: Verify battery voltage UBA ≥ 90V.
Verify RS pressure ≥ 6.5 kg/cm² on auxiliary air gauge.
Check that tap changer (GR) is at notch '0' (Lamp LSCG must be lit).
Check position of protective relays: QLM, QRSI1/2, QOP1/2, QOA.
remedial_steps: 1. Check if RS pressure is low: If below 6.5 kg/cm², start baby compressor (MCPA) using switch ZCPA until RS pressure is ≥ 7.0 kg/cm².
2. Check pilot lamp LSCG: Tap changer must be at zero notch. If LSCG is not glowing, manually check GR drum position or tap GR air motor.
3. Inspect Relay Board in corridor:
- Check target of Relay QLM (Transformer Primary Overcurrent): If dropped, reset manually by twisting target knob.
- Check Relay QRSI1 / QRSI2 (Silicon Rectifier Overcurrent): Reset if dropped.
- Check Relay QOP1 / QOP2 (Power Circuit Earth Fault): Reset if dropped.
- Check Relay QOA (Auxiliary Circuit Earth Fault): Reset if dropped.
4. Check Fuses on fuse board: Inspect CCPT (16 Amp) and CCBA (35 Amp). If blown, replace with spare fuse from fuse box.
5. Check emergency flap BVEB / BPEMS in both cabs: Ensure fully released.
6. Try closing DJ: Press BLDJ, hold BLRDJ for 4 seconds until LSDJ extinguishes and LSALT extinguishes.
7. If DJ still fails to close, wedge Relay Q44 temporarily with wooden wedge only under direct instruction from TLC (22328).

breakers_relays.name: Relay QLM
breakers_relays.function: High Tension Transformer Primary Overcurrent Relay

safety_precautions: Never wedge protective relays QLM, QRSI, or QOP. Doing so risks major transformer or rectifier fire.
contact_instruction: Inform TLC (22328) immediately if relay target dropped more than twice.

flowchart.title: Conventional WAP-4 / WAG-7 DJ Closing Decision Flowchart
flowchart.summary: Step-by-step relay sequence (Q44, Q118, Q45) and pneumatic checks when BLDJ is pressed but LSDJ remains glowing.

steps.title: DJ Not Closing (LSDJ Glowing Continuously)
steps.desc: BLDJ push button pressed, but LSDJ remains lit. DJ does not close with audible latching sound.

steps.title: Check Battery Voltage (>= 90V)
steps.desc: Check Control Battery Voltmeter. Is battery voltage equal to or higher than 90 Volts?

steps.title: Check Auxiliary Reservoir (RS) Pressure
steps.desc: Check RS pressure gauge on Pneumatic Panel. Is RS pressure >= 6.5 kg/cm²?

steps.title: Check Battery Knife Switch & CHBA
steps.desc: Check Battery Knife Switch (HOBA). Check Battery Charger (CHBA) MCB. Ensure proper terminal connection.

steps.title: Verify Relay Q44 & Q118 Positions
steps.desc: Inspect Relay Panel: Ensure Tap Changer GR is on '0' notch. Ensure Relay Q44 and Q118 are in de-energized normal state.

steps.title: Start Baby Compressor (MCPA)
steps.desc: Start Baby Compressor (MCPA) using ZCPA switch. Build RS pressure up to at least 7.5 kg/cm².

steps.title: Operate BLDJ Push Button
steps.desc: Press BLDJ firmly for 2 to 3 seconds until LSDJ extinguishes and UA line voltmeter kicks to 25 kV.

steps.title: DJ Closed Successfully
steps.desc: LSDJ extinguished. UA meter shows 25 kV. Auxiliary motors pick up. Locomotive ready for notching.

steps.title: DJ Coil / Magnet Valve Fault -> Call TLC
steps.desc: If DJ still does not close after verifying RS pressure and relays, call TLC on 22328 / PCNL on 22666.

title: DJ Tripping on 1st Notch or on Run
symptoms: DJ closes normally on notch 0, but trips the moment throttle is moved to Notch 1.
LSDJ illuminates accompanied by bell / buzzer.
Ammeter shows instantaneous heavy surge before tripping.
Relay QLM or QOP drops target.
probable_causes: Earth fault in one of the Traction Motors (TM 1 to 6).
Short circuit or flashover on Silicon Rectifier (RSI 1 or RSI 2) block.
Bogie isolation switch (HMCS 1 or HMCS 2) in wrong position.
Wheel slip relay (QD) malfunctioning and causing severe hunting.
Smoothing reactor (SL) insulation breakdown.
preliminary_checks: Check which relay target has dropped in relay panel: QLM, QRSI, or QOP.
Inspect Traction Motor commutators through inspection windows if smell of smoke is noticed.
Verify reverser (J1 / J2) is fully engaged in Forward/Reverse position.
remedial_steps: 1. Inspect relay targets in corridor to identify exact cause of tripping:
- Case A: If Relay QLM dropped -> Serious transformer primary overload. Do NOT reset without visual inspection of transformer oil level and Buchholz relay.
- Case B: If Relay QRSI dropped -> Silicon rectifier overcurrent. Check RSI block diodes and cooling blowers MVSI1/MVSI2.
- Case C: If Relay QOP1 / QOP2 dropped -> Earth fault in Traction Motor circuit.
2. If QOP dropped (Earth fault in TM circuit):
- Reset QOP target.
- Isolate Bogie-1 by placing switch HMCS-1 to '2' (isolate TM 1, 2, 3). Try taking notch 1. If DJ does not trip, fault is in Bogie-1.
- If DJ still trips, return HMCS-1 to '1' and place HMCS-2 to '2' (isolate TM 4, 5, 6).
- To pinpoint exact defective traction motor: Use individual motor cut-out switches (1, 2, 3 or 4, 5, 6) on HMCS switchboard.
3. Once the defective motor is isolated, reclose DJ, verify LSDJ extinguishes, and proceed with remaining 5 traction motors with restricted haulage load.
safety_precautions: Do not exceed notch 20 when running with one isolated traction motor. Observe motor ammeters closely on gradients.
contact_instruction: Advise TLC (22328) immediately regarding isolated traction motor number and revised train clearance plan.

flowchart.title: Conventional DJ Tripping on 1st Notch / Run Flowchart
flowchart.summary: Diagnostic sequence to identify dropped relay targets (QLM, QOP, Q20, Q44) and tap changer faults.

steps.title: DJ Trips on 1st Notch or on Run
steps.desc: Moving MP throttle to notch 1 causes DJ to trip instantly, or DJ opens while running at speed.

steps.title: Inspect Relay Target Indicators
steps.desc: Enter Machine Room and inspect target indicators on Relay Panels 1 & 2.

steps.title: Which Target has Dropped?
steps.desc: Identify the dropped safety relay target flag:

steps.title: Inspect Transformer Oil & Primary Bushing
steps.desc: QLM drop indicates transformer primary surge. Check transformer oil gauge and explosion vent. Reset QLM target once only.

steps.title: Isolate Traction Motors via HVMT
steps.desc: Earth fault detected. Rotate HVMT switch to isolate TM-1/2 or TM-3/4 or TM-5/6 one by one to pinpoint grounded motor.

steps.title: Wait for OHE Voltage Stabilization
steps.desc: Q20 drops when OHE exceeds 30 kV. Wait for tension stabilization before re-closing DJ.

steps.title: Check Control Air & Tap Changer GR
steps.desc: Ensure Control Air Pressure >= 5.0 kg/cm². Ensure tap changer GR returns freely to '0' without sticking.

steps.title: Target Reset & Traction Resumed
steps.desc: Re-close DJ. Notch up smoothly with sanding to avoid wheel slip. If trips again, contact TLC (22328).

title: Auxiliary Motors (MVRH, MVMT 1/2) Not Starting / SIV Tripping
symptoms: DJ closes, but auxiliary machines do not start.
Static Inverter (SIV) external fault lamp or QSIT relay trips.
Pilot lamp LSCHG glowing red (Battery not charging).
Pilot lamp LSVEA / LSAF glows continuously.
probable_causes: Earth fault in auxiliary machine windings detected by Relay QOA or SIV internal sensor.
Single phasing or fuse blown in 415V 3-phase auxiliary bus.
Static Inverter internal DC-link fault or cooling fan stopped.
Contactor C118 (Arno starting contactor) or QSIT relay tripped.
One auxiliary motor bearing jammed (e.g. MVRH, MVMT1, MVMT2, MVSI1, MVSI2).
preliminary_checks: Check SIV display panel in machine room for error code (e.g. Earth Fault, Overload, Under-voltage).
Check position of Relay QOA / Relay QSIT.
Inspect rotary switch HQOA (Earth Fault Isolation Switch).
remedial_steps: 1. On modern SIV fitted conventional locos, check the SIV display panel: Note down fault code.
2. Press 'Fault Reset' button on SIV front panel for 5 seconds.
3. If SIV indicates 'Earth Fault on Auxiliary Machine':
- Place switch HQOA in position '0' (Earth fault protection bypassed) strictly as per SIV troubleshooting manual.
- Start auxiliary machines one by one using individual switches on corridor panel to identify which machine is causing the earth fault.
- Isolate the defective auxiliary machine (e.g., if one compressor or one cab fan is grounded).
4. On older Arno converter locos: Check contactor C118. Ensure Arno starts and builds balanced 3-phase supply.
5. Verify that pilot lamp LSCHG extinguishes, confirming battery charger (CHBA) is operational and auxiliary machines are running.
safety_precautions: If transformer oil radiator blower (MVRH) cannot be started, loco must NOT be worked under load. Transformer will overheat within 10 minutes without MVRH.
contact_instruction: Advise TLC (22328) immediately. If MVRH is defective, ask for relief engine or attach dead loco.

flowchart.title: Conventional Auxiliary Motors & SIV Tripping Flowchart
flowchart.summary: Relay QSIT verification, SIV inverter reset, and auxiliary motor protection sequence.

steps.title: SIV Tripped / Auxiliary Motors Failed to Start
steps.desc: LSAF warning lamp glows or traction motor/oil cooling blowers (MVRH, MVMT) do not start after DJ close.

steps.title: Inspect SIV Display Unit in Machine Room
steps.desc: Read diagnostic LED display on Static Inverter (SIV) cubicle. Note fault code (Earth Fault, DC Overvoltage, or Overload).

steps.title: Press SIV Reset Push Button
steps.desc: Press SIV Reset button on SIV front panel for 3 seconds to clear transient inverter trip.

steps.title: Check Relay QSIT Position
steps.desc: Examine Relay QSIT on relay panel. Is QSIT target dropped or in normal picked-up state?

steps.title: Auxiliary Motors Running Smoothly
steps.desc: All auxiliary motors start up within 15 seconds. LSAF lamp extinguishes. Resume train working.

steps.title: Persistent SIV Fault -> Consult TLC
steps.desc: If QSIT drops repeatedly, an auxiliary motor winding may be shorted. Consult TLC (22328) for SIV bypass procedure.

title: SOP for Approaching & Coasting Through Neutral Sections (GR 17.07)
symptoms: Approaching Neutral Section warning boards.
Risk of heavy flashover / OHE damage if VCB/DJ is not opened before passing neutral section.
Severe arc drawn between pantograph and catenary wire.
probable_causes: Crew distraction or failure to call out warning boards.
DJ/VCB failure to open when BLDJ pressed.
Applying train brakes inside the neutral section causing train to stall inside dead zone.
preliminary_checks: Identify sighting of 500-metre Warning Board.
Both LP and ALP must call out: 'Neutral Section 500 Metres Ahead!'
remedial_steps: 1. At 500-Metre Warning Board: Both LP and ALP exchange loud vocal call. ALP alerts LP. Loco Pilot gradually reduces throttle / tractive effort.
2. At 250-Metre Warning Board: Bring Master Controller throttle completely to '0' position. Confirm Tractive Effort reads 0 kN.
3. At 'SWITCH OFF' Board: Press BLDJ to OPEN the Main Circuit Breaker (DJ/VCB). Verify pilot lamp LSDJ illuminates and OHE voltmeter drops to 0 kV.
4. While Coasting Through Dead Zone: STRICTLY DO NOT apply regenerative, dynamic, or train air brakes inside the neutral section to avoid stalling in the dead zone.
5. At 'SWITCH ON' Board: Press BLDJ to CLOSE the Main Circuit Breaker. Verify LSDJ extinguishes and OHE voltmeter recovers to 25 kV.
6. Slowly advance throttle notch by notch (or 10% increments on 3-Phase locos) to resume normal train speed.
7. If train stalls inside neutral section: Inform TLC (22328) / Section Controller immediately. Lower pantograph, do NOT attempt to close DJ, arrange for pushing/pulling assistance as per SR 17.07.
safety_precautions: Passing Neutral Section with DJ closed is a serious safety violation leading to severe OHE wire parting and pantograph entanglement.
contact_instruction: If loco stalls inside the neutral section, immediately protect train and call TLC (22328) & PCNL (22666 / 22667).

flowchart.title: Neutral Section Coasting Procedure (GR 17.07) Flowchart
flowchart.summary: Spatial procedural sequence from 500m warning board to clearing dead section and resuming traction.

steps.title: Sighting 500 Metres Warning Board
steps.desc: Loco Pilot sights the 500m Neutral Section Warning Board beside the track ahead.

steps.title: At 500m Board: Drop Throttle to '0'
steps.desc: Cut off tractive effort immediately. Return throttle / TE/BE handle to '0' position.

steps.title: At 250m Board: Open DJ / VCB
steps.desc: Sighting 250m Warning Board: Press BLDJ to open DJ / VCB. Confirm LSDJ glows.

steps.title: Confirm Zero OHE Voltage on U-Meter
steps.desc: Verify line voltmeter reads 0 kV while panto remains raised. Train coasts through dead section on momentum.

steps.title: Coast Past Neutral Section Cleared Board
steps.desc: Wait until locomotive pantograph completely crosses the 'Neutral Section Cleared / Resume' board.

steps.title: Emergency Lower Panto via ZPT
steps.desc: If DJ fails to open, immediately lower pantograph via ZPT switch to avoid shattering OHE insulators!

steps.title: Re-close DJ / VCB
steps.desc: Press BLDJ to re-close DJ/VCB. Confirm LSDJ extinguishes and line voltmeter indicates 25 kV.

steps.title: Resume Normal Notching
steps.desc: Notch up traction gradually. Maintain permissible sectional speed without wheel slipping.

title: Passing Automatic Stop Signal at 'ON' (GR 9.02 & SR 9.02.01)
symptoms: Automatic Stop Signal displaying RED ('ON') aspect in automatic signalling territory.
Train halted in block section behind red signal.
probable_causes: Preceding train occupied in the overlap ahead.
Track circuit failure or broken rail in the section ahead.
Signal aspect bulb burnt out or signal mechanism fault.
preliminary_checks: Bring train to a complete stop at the foot of the Automatic Stop Signal (clear of the signal post).
Observe the 'A' marker disc (letter 'A' in black on white circular disc) on the signal post.
remedial_steps: 1. Stop the train before the Automatic Stop Signal showing RED.
2. Wait for 1 MINUTE during Day time, or 2 MINUTES during Night time.
3. If the signal still does not turn green or yellow, give one long continuous whistle.
4. Exchange signals with Guard: Guard will show white light / flag to proceed with caution.
5. Move the train forward with extreme caution: Maximum speed must NOT exceed 15 km/h under clear weather, and must NOT exceed 10 km/h in thick, foggy, or tempestuous weather.
6. The Loco Pilot and ALP must maintain sharp lookout ahead, ready to stop dead short of any train, vehicle, broken rail, or obstruction.
7. Continue running at this restricted speed until the train reaches the next stop signal (even if it shows green or yellow aspect from a distance).
8. Record the signal number, time halted, and time passed in the Loco Pilot's rough journal.
safety_precautions: Strict adherence to 15 km/h (clear weather) and 10 km/h (foggy weather). Do not resume normal speed until reaching the subsequent signal.
contact_instruction: Report red automatic stop signal passing to the next Station Master on walkie-talkie and TLC (22328).

flowchart.title: Passing Automatic Stop Signal at 'ON' (GR 9.02) Flowchart
flowchart.summary: Mandatory safety timings, whistle codes, and restricted speed limits when passing an Automatic Stop Signal at Danger.

steps.title: Automatic Stop Signal Displaying 'Danger'
steps.desc: Loco Pilot sights an Automatic Stop Signal showing Red / 'ON' aspect.

steps.title: Stop Train in Rear of the Signal
steps.desc: Bring train to a complete halt before the foot of the signal. Apply loco and train brakes.

steps.title: Mandatory Halt: 1 Min Day / 2 Min Night
steps.desc: Wait exactly 1 minute by day or 2 minutes by night with train stationary.

steps.title: Whistle Code & Signal Exchange with Guard
steps.desc: Sound one long continuous whistle. Exchange hand signals (Red/Green flag or lamp) with the Guard.

steps.title: Assess Track Visibility Conditions
steps.desc: Is visibility clear, or is it impaired by fog, heavy rain, dust storm, or sharp curves?

steps.title: Proceed at Speed Not Exceeding 15 kmph
steps.desc: Start train cautiously. Maximum speed must not exceed 15 kmph. Be ready to stop short of any obstruction.

steps.title: Restrict Speed to 10 kmph or Walking Pace
steps.desc: Under impaired visibility or curve, restrict speed to 10 kmph or walking pace so train can stop within visible distance.

steps.title: Arrive at Next Stop Signal
steps.desc: Maintain cautious speed until next Stop Signal ahead is sighted. Obey its aspect strictly.

title: Foggy Weather Operation & Detonator Protection (GR 3.61)
symptoms: Visibility severely impaired by dense fog, mist, or tempestuous weather.
Signal sighting board or stop signals not visible beyond 100 metres.
Fog Signal Posts (FSP) encountered.
probable_causes: Winter dense fog conditions in Eastern Railway (Howrah / Barddhaman / Asansol sections).
preliminary_checks: Verify Fog Pass Device (FPD / GPS-based audio-visual warning device) is switched ON and calibrated in cab.
Verify loco flasher light is tested and working.
Inspect detonator box: Ensure 10 live detonators are available in cab.
remedial_steps: 1. In thick or foggy weather, turn on loco headlight on HIGH BEAM and keep marker lights ON.
2. Observe speed restrictions: Speed must NOT exceed 75 km/h in Automatic block territory and 60 km/h in Absolute block territory, or as specified in divisional caution orders.
3. Station staff will place 2 detonators, 10 metres apart, at a distance of 270 metres outside the First Stop Signal.
4. When the locomotive explodes detonators:
- Loco Pilot must immediately reduce speed, apply brakes, and be prepared to stop dead short of the Home / Outer signal.
- Sound continuous whistle code: '_ _' (two long blasts) to alert Guard and station staff.
5. Proceed with extreme vigilance only after sighting the signal aspect.

6. If train stops in section due to accident or failure during fog: Immediately protect the train in rear by placing 1 detonator at 600m and 3 detonators at 1200m (10m apart) from the obstruction as per GR 6.03.
safety_precautions: Safety takes absolute precedence over punctuality in foggy weather. Never assume a signal aspect without positive sighting.
contact_instruction: Keep in constant touch with Guard via Walkie-Talkie (Channel 1) and report dense fog zones to TLC (22328).

flowchart.title: Foggy Weather & Detonator Protection (GR 3.61) Flowchart
flowchart.summary: Visibility assessment, detonator placement distances, and speed restrictions during thick fog.

steps.title: Foggy Weather Impairing Visibility
steps.desc: Thick fog, tempestuous weather, or dust storm reduces visibility on the section.

steps.title: Station Master Visibility Test Post Check
steps.desc: Station Master checks Visibility Test Object / Post (180m from SM office). Can it be seen?

steps.title: Normal Train Working Maintained
steps.desc: Visibility is adequate. Detonator protection not required. Maintain standard sectional speeds.

steps.title: Depute 2 Fog Signalmen with 24 Detonators
steps.desc: Station Master immediately calls 2 trained fog signalmen. Issue 24 detonators each with hand signal lamps.

steps.title: Place 2 Detonators 10m Apart at 270m
steps.desc: Fog signalman places two detonators on rail 10 metres apart, at a distance of 270 metres in rear of First Stop Signal.

steps.title: Is Locomotive Equipped with Fog Safe Device (FSD)?
steps.desc: Check whether active GPS-based Fog Safe Device is provided in driver cab:

steps.title: Proceed with FSD: Max 75 kmph
steps.desc: Loco Pilot guided by FSD audio-visual countdown. Maximum speed permissible is 75 kmph.

steps.title: Proceed Without FSD: Max 60 kmph
steps.desc: Speed restricted to maximum 60 kmph. Extreme alertness: sound intermittent whistles and observe detonators.
